chart.title: Used to — past habits
rows: I used to play video games inside.
My friend didn't use to have a computer.
Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
chart.note: Use 'used to' to talk about habits or situations in the past that don't happen now. 'Used to' is different from 'be used to'. Question form: Did + subject + use to + verb?

sentences: I used to walk to school every day.
She used to have long hair.
People didn't use to have cell phones.
Did you use to play outside after school?
We used to watch black and white TV.
He didn't use to like vegetables.
Children used to learn without computers.
My grandparents used to wash clothes by hand.
Did people use to travel by horse?
I didn't use to drink coffee, but now I do.

rules.title: Positive — subject + used to + verb
rules.explanation: Use 'used to + verb' to say something happened regularly in the past but doesn't happen now.
examples: I used to play outside every day.
She used to have a pet rabbit.

rules.title: Negative — subject + didn't use to + verb
rules.explanation: Use 'didn't use to + verb' to say something did NOT happen regularly in the past.
examples: People didn't use to have electricity.
My friend didn't use to like reading.

rules.title: Question — Did + subject + use to + verb?
rules.explanation: To ask about past habits, use 'Did + subject + use to + verb?' Answer with Yes, I did or No, I didn't.
examples: Did you use to walk to school?
Did people use to travel by horse?
